title: Do LLMs Understand Network Traces? A Comparative Study of Reasoning over Raw and Filtered Traffic Data
abstract: arXiv:2611.22575v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The effective delivery and monitoring of ICT services rely heavily on network traffic analysis. However, interpreting complex packet captures remains a challenging task that requires substantial technical expertise. Large language models (LLMs) offer promising opportunities to automate network traffic in- vestigation, yet their reliability in packet-level field extraction and flow-level sequence reconstruction remains an open research question. This study proposes a reproducible, question-answering- based evaluation methodology to assess the capabilities of LLMs in network trace analysis. Using real-world benign traffic from the CICIDS2017 dataset, we evaluate multiple models against a human-generated ground truth, comparing their performance on raw textual traffic dumps and protocol-filtered representations. translated_title: 大语言模型能理解网络流量轨迹吗？一项关于原始与过滤流量数据推理能力的对比研究
translated_abstract: ICT（信息通信技术）服务的有效交付与监控在很大程度上依赖于网络流量分析。然而，解读复杂的数据包捕获仍然是一项具有挑战性的任务，需要大量的专业技术知识。大语言模型（LLMs）为自动化网络流量调查提供了有前景的机遇，但其在数据包级字段提取和流级序列重建方面的可靠性仍然是一个悬而未决的研究问题。本研究提出了一种可复现的、基于问答的评估方法，以评估大语言模型在网络流量轨迹分析方面的能力。该方法使用来自CICIDS2017数据集的真实良性流量，将多个模型与人工生成的真实标准进行对比评估，比较它们在原始文本流量转储和协议过滤表示两种形式上的表现。模型响应通过自动化的“LLM作为裁判”流水线进行评估，该流水线已经过人工评估的验证。
tldr: 本研究提出了一种可复现的、基于问答的评估方法，结合经过人工验证的“LLM作为裁判”自动化流水线，系统评估了大语言模型在网络流量轨迹分析中处理原始与协议过滤数据的推理能力。
en_tdlr: This study proposes a reproducible, question-answering-based evaluation methodology with a human-validated LLM-as-a-judge pipeline to systematically assess LLMs' reasoning capabilities over raw and protocol-filtered network traffic traces.
